Hi Patrick — thanks for the checklist and timeline. Attaching a few artifacts: a routing diagram that highlights control plane vs data plane, our filled questionnaire, and a short summary of transfer mechanisms we support. High-level answers below; see attachments for source-of-truth.

1) Default routing: Hosted requests originating in the US are served from US regions (primary: us-west-2, fallback: us-east-1). Customer-configured Dedicated/Private deployments can restrict processing to specific regions.

2) Backups/snapshots: Persistent backups are stored in the same cloud region by default; short-term replication for HA may be to a secondary region in the same geography. We do not replicate user data to EU/APAC unless explicitly configured.

3) Subprocessors: We use cloud providers (AWS) and a managed logging vendor (LogVantage Ltd.). We list subprocessors in our SCC appendix; open to sharing the vendor roster under an NDA.

4) Fallback behavior: Smart routing can failover to a secondary region for availability; this is policy-driven and can be disabled per-account. Model fallback (smaller model variant) does not change storage region but may change compute tier.

5) Transfer mechanisms: For hosted customers, we rely on SCCs (EU standard contractual clauses) where applicable; for enterprise/private deployments we support data residency commitments in contract. We provide a template DPA with SCCs embedded and an option for SCC + supplementary measures (logging controls, KMS separation).

Action items: Markus, can you confirm the managed logging vendor name and whether backups ever transit outside primary geography for customers on our hosted plan? Neha, can you attach the SCCs excerpt we provide in the DPA?

I'll upload the diagrams to the Drive link and share the HubSpot deal for reference.

Best,

Quick note to confirm: the managed logging vendor is LogVantage Ltd. We do periodic short-term replication of metrics/log windows to their EU endpoint for analytics only; production customer data backups (snapshots of customer volumes) remain in the customer region unless explicit cross-region backup is requested in the account config. For hosted plan customers like Helix Health (per current deal), default behavior will not replicate backups to EU/APAC.

If Helix needs a contract clause restricting any cross-region backup or analytic export, we can add a data residency addendum to the Dedicated/Hosted SLA.

Team — appreciate the clarifying questions. Short answers here; attachments contain the formal text we reference.

1) SCCs: We ship the EU Commission 2021 standard contractual clauses (Commission Implementing Decision 2021/914) in our standard DPA. Document excerpt is attached (sccs-summary.pdf) and the DPA template with embedded SCCs is in the Drive link.

2) Logging/PHI: Our managed logging pipeline ingests structured telemetry and operational logs. We exclude patient identifiers from logs by default (PII/PHI redaction at ingestion). For customers who opt-in to more verbose logging, we provide tokenization and hashing as supplementary measures. We can provide our ingestion redaction policy and sample logs under NDA.

3) KMS: We support both Redwood-managed KMS keys and customer-managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS. With CMKs, keys are in the customer's AWS account and Redwood never has key material or decrypt access. The KMS separation summary is attached.
